decisions.check_result: I re-read every cited line at 5999fbf. clean_filename (app.py:75-80) gives a deterministic label. analyze_video names evidence evt_{label}_{int(video_time*1000):08d}.jpg (engine.py:87-88) and writes it with cv2.imwrite into the shared EVIDENCE_DIR (engine.py:95, app.py:30). insert_event uses a global UNIQUE storage_key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (app.py:245-249, schema:186), sha256 is never set (schema:189), and /evidence checks only the row and os.path.exists before FileResponse (app.py:659-683). No control binds the file to the row's owner. I folded in the merged duplicate engine.py:analyze_video:evidence-filename-not-owner-unique, which has the same root cause (non-owner-unique evt_ names plus first-writer-wins). I added its evidence on app.py:80, engine.py:76/87 and the engine-wide ThreatScorer (engine.py:46, 83), which makes stamp collisions depend on runtime state. I moved the edge pre-claim variant to the separate /ingest record. That variant has a different missing control: accepting a client-chosen key with no proof of production. Fixing either root cause leaves the other open. The cross-owner read is a runtime claim that could not be observed: there was no sandbox, DB or model, and whether events fire at a given stamp depends on the model and scorer state. So it stays needs_validation, with an exact stub-detector local plan and a read-only owner query for video events without media rows.

merged into backend/app.py:evidence:first-claimant-storage-key-serves-shared-evidence-file. This is the same source root cause (evt_ names from the client filename and video time, shared directory, global first-writer-wins storage_key) and the same sink. It was listed as a merged duplicate of that candidate, so no separate record is produced and its evidence was folded into the surviving record.

The trace is correct: edge_from_token returns only the id and community (auth.py:214-223), validate_event checks only the image charset (app.py:71, 103-106), and insert_event stores the name as a global storage_key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, size 0 if absent (app.py:228, 240-249). A NULL camera passes the admin branch c.id IS NULL in /evidence (app.py:662-664), which serves the on-disk file (app.py:683). Edge camera_id is bound to the device (cameras.py:165-174), but no binding exists for image. The edge has no upload endpoint and the documented payload sends no image (test_ingest.py:22), so this is not design-intended. The principal is an operator-provisioned token for community A plus A's admin. The result still crosses a real boundary: another community's private evidence, or a hidden private camera's evidence in A. It also silently drops the victim's media row. The proposed confirmed verdict is demoted: the claimed result (admin of A receives victim bytes) is runtime behaviour that was not observed without a sandbox or DB, and the cross-community capture also depends on predicting a victim's upload filename. Severity was removed. It is kept as a separate fingerprint because its missing control (an unauthenticated object reference from the edge) differs from the /analyze naming root cause. The local plan reproduces it with insert_event and TestClient alone; the deployment plan is a read-only query for user_id NULL rows claiming backend or detector names.
